patch_description: Instead of computing independent per-destination Dijkstra shortest paths (which duplicates edges per partition and ignores shared structure), this approach builds a shared broadcast relay tree (Steiner-tree style): it finds a low-cost tree rooted at src that reaches all destinations, so common prefixes of paths are reused, dramatically reducing redundant edge transfers. Each partition still gets a full path per destination (traversing tree edges), but shared upstream edges only count once in overall transfer. Additionally, partitions are diversified: each partition's route to a destination is chosen from the k-shortest simple paths to balance load across parallel network links and avoid bottlenecking a single expensive path. The algorithm: (1) compute k-shortest paths per dst by cost; (2) greedily select paths that maximize overlap with already-chosen edges (prefix sharing) while keeping edge usage bounded (load balancing); (3) emit the resulting paths per (dst, partition). This reduces total cost versus naive per-partition Dijkstra replication.
